## Owner-ruled scope amendment: 8 pulled skills join the skill-sync scope

Pratik ruled 2026-11-09: add the 8 skills pulled from this repo to the live tree earlier today to the sync scope. These 8 were flagged as membership candidates by tonight's daily skill-sync run (no drift among the 82 previously in-scope skills); scope membership changes are edits to the scope file by PR, never improvised by the sync job — this is that PR.

### The 8 skills

`archify`, `neurogenesis_teams`, `ralph_loop`, `recurring-workflows`, `roundtable_review`, `teach`, `to-questionnaire`, `writing-articles`

### Diff summary (the merge evidence — read it, per the sync standard)

- `.github/skills-sync-scope.txt`: +8 lines, one insertion per skill, each at its alphabetical position in [skills] (archify after `aim`; neurogenesis_teams after `neurogenesis`; ralph_loop after `prototype`; recurring-workflows after `receiving-code-review`; roundtable_review after `reverse_engineering`; teach before `test-driven-development`; to-questionnaire after it; writing-articles before `writing-for-agents`). Nothing else in the file changes.
- `.github/skills-manifest.sha256`: regenerated in the worktree — **178 → 385 entries (+207)**; post-write `--check` passes (`OK: 385 manifest entries match the tree at skills`). The +207 is exactly the 8 skills' 215 tree files minus their 8 `skill.yaml` files, which the [exclude-paths] rule keeps out of the manifest. No `excluded (content rule)` lines; no previously listed file dropped. (The manifest is scope-filtered: the checker walks only the directories named in [skills], so a scope addition is what produces this delta.)
- No skill file is touched by this PR. Total diff: 2 files, +215/−0.

### Live == repo verification

The sync contract carries SKILL.md and FORK.md only. Hash-compared for all 8 skills before amending: **8/8 SKILL.md byte-identical** between `~/workspace/custom-skills/<skill>/` and `skills/<skill>/` (sha256). None of the 8 has a FORK.md on either side. Nothing was copied in either direction — this PR changes scope + manifest only.

### Bootstrap note — first live edit to one of these 8 (expected behaviour, stated plainly)

The sync job's drift-direction guard classifies a differing file by the newest commit on develop touching it: a sync-subject commit means live-ahead (sync proceeds); anything else means repo-ahead (the file is excluded and reported as a pull candidate for the owner's ruling). These 8 enter scope with non-sync newest-touching commits on every one of their 207 manifest files (full per-file census, panel-verified 2026-11-11): seven skills sit entirely at `1f68bed chore(skills): publish custom skills to repo (#7)`; archify's SKILL.md and `bin/*.mjs` sit at `7a15219 fix(archify): … (#32)`, its `package.json`/`package-lock.json` at `9142ae2 chore(deps-dev): … (#80)`, and its remaining 193 manifest files at `8e2006d feat(skills): vendor archify diagram skill … (#27)`. All are non-sync commits. (The 0f5b652 bootstrap anchor is skipped by the guard and does not change this — for these paths it is in fact TREESAME and never appears as a touching commit.)

Consequence (per-file, as the guard operates): **the first live edit to any one of these 207 files will surface that file once as a pull candidate** in a sync run instead of syncing automatically — up to 207 one-time events across the 8 skills (198 of them in archify), each self-extinguishing as its file's baseline lands. The resolution is the PR #132 pattern: an owner-ruled landing that copies the live file in under the standard sync subject (`chore(skills): sync vendored skill copies to the live skills`), which makes that file's newest touching commit a sync commit — from then on it classifies live-ahead and the daily sync carries it normally. Each file's baseline is established independently, on its first divergence.

This PR cannot set those baselines itself: it touches no SKILL.md, and manufacturing content changes to fake touching commits would corrupt the record. And until a live edit actually happens there is nothing to classify — live == repo is verified above, so post-merge sync runs should report no drift for these 8.

### Notes

- The daily sync job reads the scope file from origin/develop at runtime; no job change is needed — the next run after this merges simply sees 90 in-scope skills.
- Merging is gated as usual: CI green on the final head, Codex clean on that head, zero unresolved threads. The merge itself is Pratik's call.


## Adversarial panel adjudication (2026-11-11)

A three-adversary panel (manifest & scope mechanics; drift-guard & bootstrap semantics; live-tree truth) reviewed this head (`273c7c4`) read-only before merge, at the owner's direction. Verdict: **no defect in the PR's mechanics** — the manifest regeneration is byte-reproducible, the +207 arithmetic is exact, all 207 files classify non-sync (zero silent-sync, zero fail-safe-noise), live↔repo byte-identity holds across all 215 tree files, and the census arithmetic is exact (90 in scope; repo-only set unchanged). Two disclosure defects in this body were found and corrected above before merge: the bootstrap consequence was framed per skill where the guard operates per file (now stated per file), and the classifier citations covered only the SKILL.md files (now the full per-file census). Two informational items were recorded as follow-up candidates, neither a defect of this PR: the manifest checker silently passes a scope entry naming no directory (a gate-hardening candidate), and `ralph_loop`/`neurogenesis_teams` carry self-described adapted content without FORK.md markers (a fork-versioning scheme question, pre-existing on the repo copies).
